title: Book Three · Chapter 170: The Question in English
story:
During the third Friday morning, a woman brings a visitor into the workshop.

Her friend is visiting from another country. He is looking at the small wooden boxes near the front.

The woman tells Mr Sun, then shows her friend the finished pieces. Ronan brings one box to the counter for them.

The man opens his bag and takes out a few cards. He says something in English and puts the cards beside the box.

Ronan knows some words. The whole question passes too quickly.

He takes a breath.

“Please say it more slowly.”

The man smiles and starts again. This time, he points to the cards, then to the space inside.

“Is it for the cards?” Ronan asks in English.

“Yes.”

Ronan puts one card beside the box. It is shorter than the inside space.

He shows the man and gives the card back. The man asks another question, but Ronan misses the last word.

He asks him to repeat it. The woman helps with one word too.

“The catch,” she says, pointing to the small part beside the lid.

Ronan looks at it. He seems to know the sound, but he has not heard it used for a box before.

He checks the man's face.

“This part?”

The man nods and points to the closed lid.

Ronan does not try to make a longer answer. Now they are pointing to the same part. He can show it slowly.

The woman leaves them room at the counter. Mr Sun is still near enough to answer about the wood and the price.

Ronan turns the box toward the visitor before he reaches for the little metal part.

The man wants to open the lid. Ronan shows him the little catch and steps aside so he can try.

Mr Sun comes over. The woman explains the final choice while Ronan finds wrapping paper.

The man pays Mr Sun and puts his cards away. Before he leaves, he thanks Ronan in English.

“Thank you,” Ronan answers, then laughs softly at himself.

The man smiles and lifts his wrapped box.

After they leave, Ronan writes the word on a scrap. He wants to check its unfamiliar meaning in his dictionary at home.

Dad looks over at the counter.

“You understood?”

“Some. I asked him to slow down. She helped too.”

Dad nods. Ronan puts the word in his notebook and returns the spare paper to the shelf.

At twelve, Mr Sun pays his third nine yuan. His work money becomes fifty-four in all.

At home, Ronan opens the dictionary before lunch. He finds the word and reads its example twice.

The first example is about a ball. He knows that use. He turns to the next part of the same word.

Here, it is a small part of a box or a door.

Ronan looks at his own storage box near the wall. Then he writes a short example below the word.

He could hear the sound at the workshop. He needed the man's hands and his friend's help to find the meaning.

He reads the new example aloud, with a small pause after the first words. This time, he can follow the whole sentence.

Mum comes to set the table.

“A customer word?”

“A very fast customer word.”

He reads it aloud more slowly. She smiles and puts his bowl beside the book.

That afternoon, he adds a short line to his application letter about his English. He can ask simple questions. He still needs practice with the answers.

He leaves the dictionary open beside the new line and reads the whole paragraph again in his own quiet voice.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

repeat＝重复；lid＝盒盖；catch＝小扣、搭扣；unfamiliar＝不熟悉的。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan有没有假装全部听懂？他用了哪些实际办法把需求问清？
2. 顾客的钱交给谁？Ronan自己的第三周工资到账后是多少？

## 读句子

**He still needs practice with the answers.**

拆开看：He / still needs practice / with the answers.

他／还需要练习／听懂对方回答的部分。
